rows.proof: THE FY 2016 OMNIBUS BUDGET as voted at the Annual Town Meeting of 2 May 2015, pages 174-176 of the FY2016 annual town report. LINE # | ACCOUNT | Fiscal Year 2016, 91 line items in thirteen sections. The section is exactly these three pages: 173 is town meeting prose and 177 opens the Special Town Meeting of 22 August 2016. WHAT CLOSES, AND IT ALL DOES. All thirteen section totals foot their own line items EXACTLY -- Maturing Debt, Gen Govt., General Govt., Central Purchasing, Protection, Health & Sanitation, DPW, Facilities & Buildings, Solid Waste/Recycle, Assistance, Schools, Library -- and the thirteen sum to the printed `Total Omnibus $32,025,895.00` to the cent, which is also the sum of the 91 line items. Nothing here is attested and nothing is tolerated. THE FOUR `Subtotal` ROWS ARE NESTED, NOT ADDITIONAL. `Subtotal Police $1,437,982.00`, `Subtotal Fire Dept. $748,540.00`, `Subtotal Radio Watch $261,975.00` and `Subtotal Other Protection $190,493.00` sum to `Total Protection $2,638,990.00`; `Subtotal C.O.A. $111,210.00` and `Subtotal Veterans $56,500.00` sum to `Total Assistance $167,710.00`. They are recorded as section_total lines and are NOT summed. Counting a `Subtotal ...` row as a line item is what once put this year's omnibus $2.8M over its own printed total.

rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the PAGE'S OWN EMBEDDED BITMAP. pdfplumber reports 137 words of text on PDF page 186 -- all of them the warrant article prose above and below the table, NONE of them inside it -- and one DeviceRGB image 727x582 at ~85 dpi carrying the whole grid, so the TABLE is a photograph even though the page is not (rule: apply the text-layer test to the REGION the figures are in). The bitmap was taken straight out of the PDF stream; it is a raw FlateDecode DeviceRGB sample array with NO container, so `get_data()` cannot be handed to PIL and `Image.frombytes('RGB',(727,582),...)` was used with the stream's own /Width, /Height and /ColorSpace, then composited over white through its /SMask. Read at 2.8x whole and again at 6x in two four-step bands, each band carrying the Grade column pasted beside it. NO RECOGNITION WAS USED.
rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2017`, 20 grades against STEP 1 to STEP 8, 160 HOURLY rates. THE COLUMN NAMES ARE THE PRINTED HEADER, READ AND WRITTEN DOWN: `Grade | Step 1 | Step 2 | Step 3 | Step 4 | Step 5 | Step 6 | Step 7 | Step 8`. THIS PAGE PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE and there is no arithmetic on it to close, so the check is COVERAGE, declared and asserted on every run: 20 grade rows, numbered 1 to 20 without going backwards, each carrying exactly the 8 rates its printed header promises. That proves the SHAPE and not the digits, and it is weaker than arithmetic for exactly that reason. THE SECOND INSTRUMENT IS THE DOCUMENT'S OWN SECOND PRINTING. The FY2016 annual town report prints this schedule TWICE, as two DIFFERENT bitmaps: page 150 inside the warrant of the Annual Town Meeting of 5 May 2016 (721x577, sha256 60d202c1...) and page 186 inside the warrant of the Special Town Meeting of 28 November 2016 (727x582, sha256 a8fb30ef...). Both were transcribed from their own bitmap and the two readings AGREE IN 160 OF 160 CELLS, 0 disagreements -- and that is also a finding about the document: the November special town meeting reprinted the May schedule UNCHANGED. BE CLEAR WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT. It is two printings read by one reader, and the second read was not blind to the first, so it is not double-entry; what it does rule out is a defect in either stored bitmap, since two independently stored images cannot be wrong the same way. A REGULARITY, TESTED AND REPORTED, NEVER USED AS THE PROOF: the steps sit about 3% apart and it is tempting to use that as the arithmetic this page lacks. IT DOES NOT HOLD TO THE CENT. round(step_1 x 1.03^(n-1)) reproduces 95 of the 140 non-STEP-1 cells and MISSES 45; compounding step to step with rounding at each step misses 45. Every miss is a single cent, which is what makes the rule tempting and what makes it useless as a check -- an error in the cents place would survive it untouched. Nothing on the page states 3%, and the ABSENCE of the regularity is the finding. ONE TYPOGRAPHIC FEATURE, READ AND RECORDED RATHER THAN NORMALISED: the GRADE 1 row prints its eight rates with NO dollar sign -- `9.44 9.72 10.01 10.31 10.62 10.93 11.26 11.61` -- while every other row prints `$`. It is the same on both pages. The figures are stored as read; the missing sign is the document's.

rows.proof: CALENDAR YEAR 2016 WAGES, pages 198-202 of the FY2016 annual town report. Four printed columns -- SURNAME | FIRST NAME | DEPARTMENT | WAGES -- set as TWO side-by-side blocks. THE RUN PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE, so there is no arithmetic to close: this group is checked on COVERAGE, which proves the SHAPE and NOT the digits. A misread digit survives it untouched. WHAT IS DECLARED. The run is TWO INDEPENDENT ALPHABETICAL SEQUENCES, not one, and neither goes backwards: the left block runs BENOIT MATTHEW to WORMELL ERIC over 264 rows on pages 198-201, the right block runs CHARTRAND BRIAN to ZRATE SEAN over 270 rows on pages 198-202. Nothing in the document says what separates them, so they are transcribed as two groups and NOT merged -- merging would be our claim and not the town's. The key is the SURNAME ONLY, because the list is sorted by surname and first names within a surname are not ordered (BORNEMAN PENNEY precedes BORNEMAN JARED on page 198); the first name is carried in fund_name so that it cannot enter the ordering key. ROWS PRINTED PER PAGE, counted off the renders: 132, 132, 132, 96, 42 -- 534 printed rows. A count that varies cannot be declared as `rows_per_page`, so it is recorded here instead and the sequence check stands alone. PAGE 199 IS A HOLE IN THE PAGE MAP and carries a full table of 132 rows; it was never listed. THE RUN STARTS AT BENOIT, NOT AT A. Page 198 opens with `BENOIT MATTHEW FIRE 13,323.91` on its first printed line with NO column heading above it, and page 197 is blank apart from the divider `MISCELLANEOUS INFORMATION`. So the page carrying the heading and the names before BENOIT (left) and before CHARTRAND (right) IS NOT IN THE PUBLISHED REPORT. How many people that is is NOT established: the document prints no count and no total. THE DOCUMENT PRINTS 36 ROWS TWICE, and the duplication is the town's and not ours. Page 202 reprints 32 rows -- TOUSIGNANT DIANNE through WORMELL ERIC -- which page 201 already prints in its left block, before continuing WOZNY JOHN to ZRATE SEAN. Separately, the last printed line of page 198 (DUSEK JAYNE and HIRSCH KRISTEN) reprints as the first line of page 199, and the last line of page 200 (RAFFAELE AMY and SODANO JOHN) reprints as the first line of page 201. Every one is identical in surname, first name, department AND amount, and all are confirmed on the renders. So 534 printed rows are 498 distinct name-rows: the printed figures sum to $16,844,780.48 and the distinct rows to $15,662,480.79, a difference of $1,182,299.69. NEITHER IS A PAYROLL TOTAL -- the first page of the list is missing, so both are LOWER BOUNDS and neither may be published as what the town paid in calendar 2016. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: whether a duplicated row is one person paid once and printed twice, or a second payment of the same amount. Nothing in the document distinguishes them, and two figures identical to the cent are consistent with either.
